ideas.description: Base: E064 code (a1aef09), which is the E062 tip (static shapes, max(dim).values pool, Muon floor 0.05, vectorized dirac, fused fp16 normalization, head Muon lr 0.5x) running E047's 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 schedule. Change only the length of the 24 px phase, from 1.5 to 1.25 epochs: 2@16 + 1.25@24 + 4@32 px, 7.25 total epochs, with step-indexed switches. Rescale the LR warmup/decay, Muon floor, EMA, lookahead and renorm cadence to the new total step count, the same way E047/E064 did. All shapes are already warmed up in build. Score it twice and log the source hash.
ideas.expected: Time about 4.57-4.60 s: removing 0.25 of a 24 px epoch (~0.125 s at bs 1536) from E064/E065's 4.71 s gives -1.5 to -2% against the 4.669 s tip. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7538-0.7550, i.e. about -0.05 to -0.12 pp against the E064/E065 pool of 0.7552, using the ~0.03-0.04 pp per 1% trim rate. If the pool is >=0.7540 (H4 rule), this becomes the new tip. If the pool is <=0.7530, the 24 px bridge is binding at 1.5 epochs and the reshuffle's accuracy gain cannot be resold as time.

ideas.description: Base: E064 code (a1aef09; 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 on the E062 tip). Trim the 16 px phase instead of the bridge: 1.5@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px, 7.0 total epochs, with step-indexed switches. Rescale LR warmup/decay, Muon floor, EMA, lookahead and renorm to the new total step count as in E064. The warmup stays the same fraction of steps. Change nothing else and score it twice. This is the sister arm of the 24 px trim at about equal time. E064/E065 versus the tip showed that 24 px time buys accuracy at ~0.13 pp per 1% and 16 px time does not, so the 16 px phase may be the cheapest one to cut.
ideas.expected: Time about 4.57-4.60 s, about -2% against the tip. Removing half a 16 px epoch saves ~0.13 s, which is similar to the 24 px trim arm. Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7535-0.7552. If it is >=0.7540 and at least equal to the 24 px-trim arm's pool, the 16 px phase is the cheapest place to cut, and 1@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 comes next. A pool <=0.7525 supports H8: the early phase needs its update count.

ideas.description: Rebased I074. Base: E062 code (the current tip, head Muon lr 0.5x). Apply Fable's tail at equal total steps. The Muon and SGD LR decay reaches its floor (0.05x for Muon, unchanged for SGD) about 4% of steps early and holds there until the end. Over the last ~8 steps, update a light final EMA every 4 steps (ema = 0.7*ema + 0.3*net via torch._foreach_lerp_; buffers allocated in build and reset in prepare). It replaces the end of the lookahead-EMA ramp, and evaluation uses those EMA weights with BN buffers copied from the net. Change nothing else, and score it twice.
ideas.expected: Time within 0.5% of the tip (4.65-4.70 s). Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7525-0.7555 against the tip pool of 0.7537 (E062/E063/E067). A pool >=0.7550 (+0.13 pp) makes it a zero-cost margin source that can then be stacked onto the winning schedule trim. A pool within ±0.1 pp of 0.7537 closes end-of-schedule tuning for Muon, along with E057.

ideas.description: Base: E062 code (head Muon lr 0.5x). Add decoupled weight decay to the Muon head weight [100, 576] only, at hiverge's bs-1536 scale: each step w -= lr_head_t * wd * w, with wd chosen so that wd*lr is about 1.6e-3 at peak, applied inside the compiled Muon update through a 0-d tensor so nothing recompiles. Leave the head bias, the filters and all schedules unchanged. Score it twice.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7525-0.7555 against the tip pool of 0.7537. A pool >=0.7550 supports H7.3.3, confirms that the head's update scale and norm are the live knob, and gives margin. A pool within ±0.12 pp closes head regularization, and with E062/E063 the head line is finished.

ideas.description: Rebased I075. Base: E062 code (head Muon lr 0.5x of filter lr). Change only the conv-filter peak Muon LR from 0.24 to 0.28 through the existing 0-d tensor. Keep the head's absolute peak LR at 0.12 (i.e. set its multiplier to 0.12/0.28) so that this run changes the filters only. Score it twice.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Two-run pooled accuracy 0.7520-0.7550. A pool >=0.7550 means the bs-1536 / ~256-step regime wants a larger filter step, which is a margin source. A pool within ±0.15 pp of 0.7537 means the bs-1024 optimum transfers, and filter Muon lr is closed. A pool <=0.7520 means 0.24 is at or above the optimum.

ideas.description: Observational, untimed. On the E062 tip code, build three variants with group-2 widths 384, 352 and 320 (recompiled and warmed up in a side script). Use CUDA events and torch.profiler on 20 steps each at 32 px and 24 px, bs 1536. Record per-layer conv fwd/bwd time, elementwise time for group 2 and group 3's conv1, and total step time and energy (NVML). For the scored row, rerun the E062 code unchanged as a fourth tip-family variance sample (log weight checksums and source hash).
ideas.expected: Scored row about 4.67 s, accuracy 0.752-0.755, which adds to the tip pool (currently 0.7537 over 3 runs). Profile prediction: 352 recovers <=60% of its FLOP-proportional group-2 time, while 320 recovers >=80%, i.e. tile misalignment explains E050's shortfall. If 320 also recovers <80%, width cuts are dead and H2.13 is refuted. If it recovers >=80%, a 320-width arm combined with the 2@16 + 1.5@24 reshuffle becomes worth one scored run.

ideas.description: Explore. On the E062 tip code, replace BN(train) + GELU in the group-2 and group-3 blocks (32/24 px shapes only) with a custom torch.autograd.Function built from two Triton kernels. The forward computes per-channel stats with one reduction pass, then applies the BN affine and exact-erf GELU in one pass, saving only the fp16 pre-BN input and the per-channel mean/rstd. The backward recomputes the normalized value and GELU' on the fly in one fused reduction (dgamma, dbeta, sum terms) plus one apply pass. Register it so torch.compile treats it as an opaque op (allow_in_graph or a custom_op), and warm up every shape in build. Before scoring, check numerics against the compiled reference on one batch (max abs grad diff at fp16 level) and confirm the loss stays finite for 10 steps. Write down the predicted bytes moved per layer first.
ideas.expected: Time -1 to -3% (about 4.53-4.62 s) if it removes >=1 full activation pass per layer in the energy-bound 24/32 px phases. Accuracy within noise (two-run pool >=0.7525), since the math is equivalent up to fp16 rounding. If time drops <0.5%, or the opaque op breaks Inductor's conv-epilogue fusions and time rises, H2.16 is closed.

drop.reason: Stale base: it targets the E060 code, but the tip is now the E062 code (head Muon lr 0.5x, pool 0.7537). Re-proposed rebased on the E062 tip so a positive result stacks directly.

Stale base, and it is confounded with the head LR: on the E060 code the head's absolute LR would rise with the filter LR. Re-proposed on the E062 tip with the head's absolute LR held at 0.12, so only the filter LR changes.

structured_output.summary:
The tip is the E062 code: 4.669-4.680 s, with a pooled accuracy of 0.7537 over 3 runs, only ~0.07 pp above the 0.753 gate. The clearest open lead is E064/E065. The 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 reshuffle pooled 0.7552 at 4.71 s, buying accuracy at ~0.13 pp per 1% of time, while trims cost only ~0.03-0.04 pp per 1%.

The two top exploit ideas resell that accuracy as time. They are a matched pair of ~-2% trims on the E064 code:
- **Priority 5:** shorten the 24 px phase to 1.25 epochs (2@16 + 1.25@24 + 4@32, ~4.58 s).
- **Priority 4:** shorten the 16 px phase to 1.5 epochs (1.5@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32, ~4.58 s).

Each is scored twice and needs a two-run pool >=0.7540 to become the tip. Comparing the two also shows which phase is cheapest to cut.

Three zero-cost margin sources come next, all on the current tip: Fable's held-floor tail plus short final EMA (rebased I074), decoupled weight decay on the Muon head, and filter Muon lr 0.28 with the head's absolute LR held fixed (rebased I075, now without the head-LR confound).

Two explore ideas follow. One is an untimed per-layer width profile (384/352/320) that gates any further width cut and also adds a variance sample to the tip pool. The other is a hand-fused Triton BN+GELU kernel, the last untested elementwise lever after E066's kernel-tuning null.

I dropped I074 and I075 only because their base is stale; both are re-proposed on the E062 tip. The queue now holds 7 ideas.
